posts.title: Rainbow Drift
posts.description: What: Nothing here moves. Not one pixel. Every shape just sits there changing colour, and yet the arrows slide, the fish swim off and the vortex sucks you in. It’s a follow-up to my Reverse Phi Rainbows, same trick, just a whole lot more of it. The whole thing is inspired by jagarikin [1], a Japanese artist who posts these on X, and his running joke is sticking an arrow on everything.

posts.title: Expanding Hole
posts.description: What: Stare at the black hole. Give it a few seconds. It’s growing, right? Like you’re falling in. It’s not, the image is totally still. It’s by Akiyoshi Kitaoka (pronounced key-TAH-oh-kah), and in 2022 some researchers showed it to 50 people and watched their eyes [1]. The wild part: your pupils fall for it too. posts.title: Motion-Induced Blindness
posts.description: What: Three big, bright yellow dots. Not faint, not tiny, not hiding. And yet, stare at the middle for a few seconds and they just… leave. Sometimes one at a time, sometimes two, sometimes all three at once. This one was found by Yoram Bonneh, Alexander Cooperman and Dov Sagi at the Weizmann Institute in 2001 [1].
